text: f. Suppose cach puppy delivers $42 in benefits to the owner’s neighbors. What is the socially optimal price and quantity of puppies? Answer: P=18, Q=324 g What are some ways in which this higher quantity of puppies could be achieved? Answer: We could think of private solutions or policy solutions. A private solution would be for neighbors to bargain among themselves and pay each other 10 buy a puppy. This is the type of solution described by the Coase Theorem, which states that this will work s long as transaction costs are low, property rights are well defined, and the number of agents bargaining is not too large. An example of a policy solution would be a Pigouvian subsidy that causes consumers to “internalize the externality.”
